step1_analysis.circuit_type: Bias Circuit for RF Power Amplifier
step1_analysis.description: A bias voltage generator circuit that provides a stable, low-impedance DC bias for an RF power amplifier or mixer. It uses a diode-connected reference branch (Q2/Q3) and an emitter/source follower (Q4) to supply bias current without loading the reference.

paper_reference.title: A Silicon Bipolar Transmitter Front-End for 802.11a and HIPERLAN2 Wireless LANs

power_consumption.description: Total DC power consumption of the bias circuit

sky130_expected.calculation: I1 is set to 100uA. M4 branch draws ~70uA. Total current ~170uA. Power = 1.8V * 170uA = 306uW. Note: The paper's 2W figure is for the entire transmitter PA, not just this bias sub-block.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Calculated based on 1.8V supply and estimated branch currents for the bias core.

v_bias_n2.description: DC bias voltage output at node n2

sky130_expected.calculation: M2/M3 set V(n0) to ~2*Vgs (~1.14V). M4 acts as a source follower, dropping ~0.5V. M1 is diode-connected, setting V(n2) to ~0.55V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Standard Vgs for diode-connected NMOS in SKY130 at moderate inversion.

startup_time.description: Time for the bias voltage at n0 to settle

sky130_expected.calculation: C1 (1pF) is charged by I1 (100uA). dt = C * dV / I = 1pF * 0.9V / 100uA = 9ns.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Based on RC/IC charging dynamics of the reference node.

gain.description: Power gain (Applies to the main PA, not this bias sub-circuit)

sky130_expected.reasoning: This is a DC bias circuit, so RF gain is not applicable.

capacitance.description: Filter capacitance at the reference node

sky130_expected.calculation: Set to 1pF in testbench for realistic filtering.
sky130_expected.reasoning: 0.7 fF is too small for a low-frequency bias filter; 1pF is more typical for on-chip bias decoupling.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC bias voltages, power consumption, and startup time of the bias circuit. Bipolar transistors are mapped to SKY130 NMOS equivalents.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Bias Circuit Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}/libs.tech/ngspice/sky130.lib.spice" tt

.param W_m1=5u L_m1=0.15u
.param W_m2=5u L_m2=0.15u
.param W_m3=5u L_m3=0.15u
.param W_m4=10u L_m4=0.15u
.param R1_val=1k R2_val=1k C1_val=1p I1_val=100u

VVDD VDD 0 1.8
I1 VDD n0 {I1_val}

* Mapped NPNs to NMOS for SKY130 CMOS evaluation
M1 n2 n2 0 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_m1} l={L_m1}
R1 n0 n3 {R1_val}
R2 n2 n4 {R2_val}
M2 n0 n0 n1 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_m2} l={L_m2}
M3 n1 n1 0 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_m3} l={L_m3}
C1 n0 0 {C1_val}
M4 VDD n3 n4 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_m4} l={L_m4}

.control
* DC Operating Point
op
let power = -i(VVDD) * 1.8
print v(n2) v(n4) power

* Transient Analysis for Startup
tran 0.1n 50n
meas tran v_n2_steady avg v(n2) from=30n to=50n
meas tran v_n4_steady avg v(n4) from=30n to=50n
meas tran t_startup trig v(n0) val=0.1 rise=1 targ v(n0) val=1.0 rise=1
let pwr_tran = -i(VVDD) * 1.8
meas tran avg_power avg pwr_tran from=30n to=50n

quit
.endc
.end
